title: add nir_opt_peephole for Intel GPUs

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body: Hello :kissing: - Closes #118719 ## Problem space With #118719. Texture's alpha channel check results in "discard", "discard" results in non uniform control flow, combined with later "while" loops causes terrible EU hang: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5ec4857b340b6284a18b49b2eda462bd250f219a/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_clustered/scene_forward_clustered.glsl#L1354-L1356 Intel PRM workarounds have an entry targeting this issue. From https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/graphics-for-linux/developer-reference/1-0/overview.html: Confirmed by: - Commenting out the "discard" solves the issue. - Disabling every "while" loop also solves the issue. ## Solution In spirv->nir->dxil chain we can place optimizations that will make more uniform control flow. Mesa nir tools already have a bunch of usefull optimizations that can help. In our case thats `nir_opt_peephole_select`. `nir_opt_peephole_select` does eliminate small if/else statements. Lets compare dxil before and after, this corresponds to the glsl code above: I did some tests and determined that exactly this change prevents the hang from #118719. From attached dxil_***.txt: - Absolutely unnecessary "if/else" branching gets compiled into dedicated `dx.op.discard` with embedded condition. [dxil_original.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31608597/dxil_original.txt) [dxil_optimized.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31608598/dxil_optimized.txt) Original nir and nir after `nir_opt_peephole_select`, search for "demote", [SceneForwardClusteredShaderRD_18_nir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31608655/SceneForwardClusteredShaderRD_18_nir.txt) [SceneForwardClusteredShaderRD_18_opt_nir.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31608661/SceneForwardClusteredShaderRD_18_opt_nir.txt) ## Debates - Maybe nir_opt_peephole_select should be enabled generaly ? It is overall a good optimization that shouldn't break shader code. - Or we can make it more conservative and restrict condition even more like: `if(use_nir_peephole_select && shader_name.contains("SceneForwardClusteredShaderRD") && shader_type == FRAGMENT)` - Also i did move instance of DriverWorkarounds to RenderingDeviceCommons. Making the instance available from anything that inherits RenderingDeviceCommons like RenderingDeviceDriver and RenderingShaderContainer so the workarounds can be used more widely. Thus future workarounds can be implemented conveniently. Or i can just make an instance of DriverWorkarounds at every class that needs it ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
